summary: refactor(core)!: the release after v0.9.0, in three parts. (1) Graph node types are deployment resources: `agent.Engine/graph` registers no type of its own and takes them as `node_type` (or `node_type.<suffix>`) deps, so a graph can only use the node kinds a document mounts; `inference`, `tool` and `script` are `graph.NodeType` resources that declare the collaborators their nodes call, `script_runtime_name` is gone in favour of `script_runtime.<name>` deps picked per node by `config.runtime`, `graph.NodeType/script` (source in the resource) became `script_inline` while `script` means the generic impl whose source comes from each node's config, and the config checks moved into `graph.NodeType[C].ValidateConfig` — called at Build per node — so a missing `model`, an unmounted runtime or a tool the catalog does not have is reported naming the node, the type and the dep to add; `graph.TypeNameProvider` backs the mounting diagnostics, and a graph naming an unmounted type fails Build listing the types that exist. (2) Checkpoints are written incrementally: `Board` records its writes, so `Board.Mark`/`Board.Since` hand a consumer a `BoardDelta` (the vars written and messages appended since a position) instead of a copy of the state — the basis of every saving below, and the contract it rests on is now explicit: a value stored in a var is immutable once written (change it with `SetVar`; mutating a value read back from `Var` was already a data race against any snapshot or parallel branch, and `agent.AuditBoardValues(true)` copies on read so a test catches it). `agent.CheckpointJournal` (`WriteBase`/`Append`) lets a store keep a base record plus append-only increments; `CheckpointStore.Load` keeps its signature and returns the rebuilt record, `backends/checkpoint/sqlite` stores increments in a second table and replays them on load (a gap is `errdefs.NotAvailable`, not partial state), and `agent.CheckpointWriter` owns the base-versus-increment decision with the compaction window from the new `build.checkpoint_compaction` (default 32). A store that only implements `CheckpointStore` keeps receiving full records. `agent.CheckpointTarget` is the optional Host capability that reports whether the host persists anything and whether it takes increments, which is what stops a deployment without a checkpoint store from snapshotting the board at every wave; `graph`, `a2a` task boundaries and `runtime/session` turn state all stamp through the writer, so the session no longer stores a second copy of the board the run checkpoint already holds, a node retry keeps one rollback point per node only when `max_node_retries > 0` (it used to snapshot per attempt and never read the result), and parallel branches hand the merge a `BranchResult.Delta` instead of one board copy each (`Snapshot` is still populated for a custom `ParallelConfig.Merge`). Along the way: `ImagePart`/`AudioPart`/`VideoPart` clones no longer share their inline media buffer with the board, and the sqlite store binds the encoded record instead of converting it to a string, cutting a record encode from 8.25x to 3.25x of its payload. (3) The review items that came with them: `errorlint`, `gocyclo` (complexity 40, baseline-only-shrinks) and a source-scanning test for `errors.New(err.Error())` join the lint gate, 218 `%v` verbs in the classified constructors became `%w` so `errors.As` can walk to the cause — which is a wire-visible change, since `errdefs.HTTPStatus` now answers from the most specific class on the chain (a NotFound inside a Validationf is 404, not 400) — and `core/errdefs` stopped re-exporting the standard library (`Is`, `As`, `Unwrap`, `Join`, `New`, `Fmt` are gone; use `errors` and `fmt.Errorf`). Configuration errors replace panics: `kanban.New`, `middleware.ResultLimiter`/`ResultPartLimiter`/`Concurrency` return `(value, error)` with `Must*` variants, `workspace.MustWorkspaceFrom` is removed, and `concurrency.limit` must be positive when the block is present instead of being silently dropped. Panic recovery in the tool middleware is on by default (`recover: {enabled: false}` opts out, `RecoverSettings.Enabled` is a `*bool`) and an assembly with no `middlewares` block now gets the default chain; the fan-out boundaries recover on their own too — `tool.Executor.Execute` turns an escaping panic into an `IsError` result, a parallel graph branch fails its branch and the wave, and a panicking sink `OnDelta` is reported as the delivery failure it is — and the recover points that used to swallow a panic now carry the run identity, the hook and the stack, under one attribute name (`telemetry.AttrCodeStacktrace`). `Runtime.Reload` applies the new `sessions` tunables in the commit phase, just before the epoch swap, so an aborted reload leaves the serving generation under its own limits, and it reports what a drain cost: a warning per drained agent plus `drained_agents` on `runtime.rebuild.failed`; a removal that removed the sessions and then failed to close them counts as drained. The keychain store is one handle per directory: every store opened over one directory in a process shares one backend and one lock (the deployment resource and the app-side manager used to hold their own locks over one accounts.json and could drop an index entry), `NewStore` resolves the directory to an absolute path with symlinks resolved and matches a second spelling by file identity, and opening a directory that already has a store re-reads its key from disk — the key file is the source of truth, and the adopted key waits for the operations running under the old one. `backends/secret` folded into `core/secret/keychain` (the `impl: keychain` deployment id is unchanged; the Go import path moved). Delegation run ids are keyed by the delegation id instead of the stream escrow ref, so a delegation that inherited no sink keeps its run id; terminal responses carry `delegation.run_id` in metadata beside `delegation.session_id` (both are telemetry constants now), `Board.Complete` copies it onto the card, `delegation.WithWorkID` supplies the claimed id for a queue-owned worker, and `SubagentStart` fires once per claim instead of once per claimed snapshot. `usage.InputTokenUsage.Validate` became `ValidateFor(inputTokens int64)`: a modality breakdown is a subset of the prompt, so its sum must not exceed the total (under-reporting stays valid) and a zero total reads as unreported, which is what an audio response billed per token looks like. Naming: `core/utils` split into `core/utils/decode` and `core/utils/httpkit` (`utils.NewHttpClient` → `httpkit.NewHTTPClient`; the root package is gone, so `core/utils` is a directory of packages), `core/utils/net` became `core/utils/netpolicy` (the package name shadowed the standard library), the doc-only `core/media` package is removed, the token/cost vocabulary sank to the leaf `core/inference/usage` (old spellings stay as aliases in `core/inference`, pinned leaf-shaped by depguard), and `Board.GetVar`/`GetVarString` became `Board.Var`/`VarString` (the script globals `board.getVar`/`board.hasVar` are unchanged). Packages that had real API surface but no contract comment (`tool`, `tool/middleware`, `runtime/session`, `graph/nodes/script`, `utils/netpolicy/mitm`) now have one, and eight hand-rolled `sortedKeys` copies plus three retry loops that leaked `time.After` timers are gone. Migration guides: `docs/migrations/core-v0.10.0.md` (panic recovery, keychain, reload, run ids, `ValidateFor`, error wrapping, checkpoints) and `docs/migrations/keychain-into-core.md`; the store contract and the compaction knob are documented in `docs/guides/checkpoint.md`.
